actor: A person who performs roles in movies or plays.
apple: A crunchy fruit that keeps the doctor away in an old saying.
arrow: What you shoot from a bow.
brain: The organ you're using to solve this puzzle.
bread: Baked from dough and sliced for sandwiches.
chair: Furniture with four legs and a back, made for sitting.
cloud: A white or gray shape floating in the sky.
crane: A tall bird on long legs, or a machine that lifts heavy loads.
daisy: A white flower with a yellow center.
diary: A private book where you write about your day.
dough: A soft mix of flour and water before baking.
dream: A story your mind tells while you sleep.
eagle: A large bird of prey and a U.S. national symbol.
earth: The third planet from the sun.
elbow: The joint in the middle of your arm.
ember: A glowing piece of coal left after a fire.
enemy: Someone who is against you; the opposite of a friend.
equal: The same in amount or value.
essay: A short piece of writing for a class.
event: Something that happens, like a concert or a game.
flame: The bright, hot part of a fire.
frost: Thin ice that forms on grass on cold mornings.
giant: A huge person in fairy tales.
glove: Something you wear on your hand in winter.
grape: A small fruit that grows in bunches and can become wine.
heart: It pumps blood through your body.
honey: A sweet, sticky food made by bees.
horse: An animal people ride, with a mane and hooves.
hotel: A place travelers pay to stay overnight.
house: A building where a family lives.
ideal: The best you can imagine; a perfect example.
igloo: A dome-shaped house made of snow blocks.
ivory: The hard white material of elephant tusks.
kayak: A narrow boat you paddle with a double-bladed oar.
knife: A kitchen tool with a sharp blade.
koala: A tree-climbing Australian animal that eats eucalyptus.
label: A sticker that tells you what's inside.
light: What a lamp gives off; the opposite of dark.
maple: A tree whose sap becomes a sweet syrup.
medal: A metal disk awarded to a winner.
melon: A big, juicy fruit like cantaloupe.
money: Coins and bills you use to buy things.
mouse: A small rodent, or the thing you click with.
nerve: A fiber that carries signals between your brain and body.
night: The dark hours between sunset and sunrise.
north: The direction a compass needle points.
novel: A long, made-up story in a book.
nurse: A hospital worker who cares for patients.
ocean: A huge body of salt water, like the Atlantic.
olive: A small green or black fruit pressed for oil.
onion: A layered vegetable that can make you cry.
opera: A play where all the words are sung.
orbit: The curved path of a moon around a planet.
paint: Colored liquid you brush onto a wall or canvas.
party: A celebration with friends, food and music.
pearl: A shiny gem formed inside an oyster.
piano: A keyboard instrument with 88 black and white keys.
pizza: A baked flatbread with cheese and toppings.
plant: A living thing that grows from soil and needs sunlight.
queen: A female ruler, or the most powerful chess piece.
radio: A device for listening to broadcasts and stations.
ranch: A large farm for raising cattle or horses.
rhyme: When two words end with the same sound.
river: Fresh water flowing toward the sea.
robot: A machine that can carry out tasks on its own.
salad: A dish of mixed greens and vegetables.
scarf: A long piece of cloth worn around the neck.
sheep: A farm animal kept for its wool.
shell: The hard outer covering of a snail or a clam.
shirt: Clothing with sleeves and buttons, worn on the top half.
smile: What your face does when you're happy.
storm: Heavy rain, wind and maybe thunder.
sugar: Sweet white crystals you add to coffee.
swamp: Wet, muddy land where alligators may live.
table: Furniture with a flat top where you eat.
toast: Bread browned in a toaster, or a speech before a drink.
torch: A flaming stick carried to give light.
train: A vehicle that runs on rails.
tulip: A cup-shaped spring flower, famous in the Netherlands.
udder: The part of a cow that milk comes from.
vapor: Tiny drops of liquid floating in the air, like steam.
water: A clear liquid you drink; H2O.
whale: The largest animal in the ocean.
wheat: A grain used to make flour.
world: All the countries and people on the planet.
yacht: A fancy boat used for sailing or cruising.
yeast: A tiny fungus that makes bread dough rise.
yield: A traffic sign that means let others go first.
youth: The time of life when you're young.
zebra: A horse-like animal with black and white stripes.
